# Wikantik Configuration Reference

Every setting Wikantik reads, with its shipped default. The defaults file
`wikantik-main/src/main/resources/ini/wikantik.properties` is the source of
this page and is complete by construction (`ConfigSurfaceDriftTest`).

## How a value is resolved

1. **Shipped defaults** — `ini/wikantik.properties` inside the wikantik-main jar. Every key below is declared there.
2. **Environment variables** whose name starts with `wikantik`, with `_` read as `.` — `PropertyReader.loadWebAppProps`. The name must match the key in **exact case** (`wikantik_baseURL`, not `WIKANTIK_BASE_URL`); the Docker image's `WIKANTIK_*` variables work because `docker/entrypoint.sh` rewrites them into the custom properties file.
3. **`wikantik-custom.properties`** on the container classpath (`tomcat/lib/`), or the file named by the `wikantik.custom.config` servlet init-param.
4. **Cascade files** `wikantik.custom.cascade.1`, `.2`, … named in the custom file.
5. **`${…}` expansion** against system properties and environment.
6. **JVM system properties** starting with `wikantik` (`-Dwikantik.foo=bar`) override everything above.

Readers that go through `TextUtil.get*Property` additionally consult the system property and the exact-case environment variable **at read time**, before the merged set, so `-D` and `wikantik_foo` win for those keys even when set after startup. Keys marked *`-D` only* are never read from the properties files at all.

`mcp.*` keys live in a separate file: `wikantik-mcp.properties` in the wikantik-admin-mcp jar, overlaid by a copy in `tomcat/lib/`.

`tools.*` keys live in a third file: `wikantik-tools.properties` in the wikantik-tools jar, overlaid by a copy in `tomcat/lib/`.

Blank values mean "unset"; the **Default** column says what the code derives in that case. `secret` keys never ship a value.

The following settings come from `wikantik-main/src/main/resources/ini/wikantik.properties` (the primary settings surface: bundled in the wikantik-main jar, overridden via the precedence chain described above).

## General

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.applicationName` | `string` | `Wikantik` | `wikantik_applicationName` | This is the Wikantik configuration file.  You'll need to edit this a bit.  The first few lines are the most important ones. If you don't want to edit this file, you can override each individual property by specifying the property name as a standard Java System Property. Wherever it is said that an option can be "true" or "false", you can also use "yes"/"no", or "on/off".  Just for some convenience. You can use this to override the default application name.  It affects the HTML titles and logging, for example.  It can be different from the actual web name (http://my.com/mywiki) of the application, but usually it is the same. |
| `wikantik.baseURL` | `url` | *(blank: falls back to the request's own scheme/host/context path)* | `wikantik_baseURL` | The public base URL of this wiki instance (e.g. https://wiki.example.com), used to build absolute URLs for SSO callback redirects, MCP sitemap/ structured-data/IndexNow tools, and connector OAuth redirect URIs. Engine. getBaseURL() only returns the servlet context path, not a full origin. (BaseUrlResolver's 3-tier fallback), or to the context path alone where no request is available (e.g. SSO callback URL construction). |
| `wikantik.templateDir` | `string` | `default` | `wikantik_templateDir` | Directory holding the wiki's skin/template. "default" ships with Wikantik. |
| `wikantik.storeIPAddress` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_storeIPAddress` | If true, then the IP address of the editor is stored with the page data. |
| `wikantik.storeUserName` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_storeUserName` | If true, then the user name will be stored with the page data. |
| `wikantik.provider.impl.acls` | `class` | `com.wikantik.spi.AclsSPIDefaultImpl` | `wikantik_provider_impl_acls` | SPI provider implementations (com.wikantik.api.spi.Wiki). Override only if you are supplying a custom implementation of the AclsSPI interface; the default is Wikantik's own. |
| `wikantik.provider.impl.contents` | `class` | `com.wikantik.spi.ContentsSPIDefaultImpl` | `wikantik_provider_impl_contents` | Override only if you are supplying a custom implementation of the ContentsSPI interface; the default is Wikantik's own. |
| `wikantik.provider.impl.context` | `class` | `com.wikantik.spi.ContextSPIDefaultImpl` | `wikantik_provider_impl_context` | Override only if you are supplying a custom implementation of the ContextSPI interface; the default is Wikantik's own. |
| `wikantik.provider.impl.engine` | `class` | `com.wikantik.spi.EngineSPIDefaultImpl` | `wikantik_provider_impl_engine` | Override only if you are supplying a custom implementation of the EngineSPI interface; the default is Wikantik's own. |

## Page storage

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.pageProvider` | `enum(FileSystemProvider\|VersioningFileProvider)` | `VersioningFileProvider` | `wikantik_pageProvider` | Which page provider class to use.  Possibilities are: FileSystemProvider     - for simple pure file storage with no version information VersioningFileProvider - for simple pure file storage with    version information |
| `wikantik.pageNameComparator.class` | `class` | *(blank: Java's natural String ordering (the default described above).)* | `wikantik_pageNameComparator_class` | How to order pages in various lists and plugins.  By default, they are ordered using Java's "natural" String order (purely character by character comparison). This means that the pages named "Page1", "Page2" and "Page10" appear in the order "Page1", "Page10", "Page2". To specify a different ordering, give the fully qualified name of a String Comparator. If the class can't be found, an error will be logged and page sorting will fall back to the default "natural" ordering. You can specify any String Comparator class here BUT be careful of using case insensitive comparators as Wikantik page names may be case sensitive. Example: wikantik.pageNameComparator.class = my.fully.qualified.comparator For convenience, we have provided a few possibly useful comparators: HumanComparator understands numbers and sorts in a more human friendly order (English only).  Using HumanComparator, the pages "Page1", "Page2", "Page10" will sort in that order. Example: wikantik.pageNameComparator.class = HumanComparator LocaleComparator uses the server's Locale for ordering.  Useful if your content is always in a language other than English.  Does not do human friendly numeric ordering. Example: wikantik.pageNameComparator.class = LocaleComparator |
| `wikantik.fileSystemProvider.pageDir` | `path` | *(blank: a "wikantik-files" directory in the user's home folder.)* | `wikantik_fileSystemProvider_pageDir` | Determines where wiki files are kept for FileSystemProvider i.e.: Example: wikantik.fileSystemProvider.pageDir = /p/web/www-data/wikantik/ If you're using Windows, then you must duplicate the backslashes. For example, use: Example: wikantik.fileSystemProvider.pageDir = C:\\Data\\jspwiki |
| `wikantik.versioningFileProvider.cacheSize` | `int` | `100` | `wikantik_versioningFileProvider_cacheSize` | Number of page.properties entries VersioningFileProvider keeps in memory. Set to 0 for single-entry, -1 for no caching. |
| `wikantik.lockExpiryTime` | `int` | `60` | `wikantik_lockExpiryTime` | Set this to the number of minutes a person can "lock" a page for while he is editing it. |
| `wikantik.systemPages.extraPatterns` | `list` | *(blank: no additional system-page patterns.)* | `wikantik_systemPages_extraPatterns` | Comma-separated regular expressions naming additional system/template pages, beyond the built-in template-directory discovery. |
| `wikantik.systemPages.mcpEditable` | `list` | `About` | `wikantik_systemPages_mcpEditable` | Comma-separated, exact system-page names that remain editable via the MCP update_page tool despite being system pages. |

## Caches

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.cache.enable` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_cache_enable` | Set to true, if you want to cache page data into memory.  This is in general a good idea. Default is true (use cache). NB: This replaces the Wikantik 1.x "CachingProvider" setting, since it probably was too confusing. |
| `wikantik.cache.allPagesTTL` | `int` | `300` | `wikantik_cache_allPagesTTL` | TTL (in seconds) of the CachingProvider's "all pages" cache. When this TTL expires, the next call to getAllPages() refreshes from the underlying provider, allowing detection of externally added or removed pages. |
| `wikantik.cache.watcherEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_cache_watcherEnabled` | Whether CachingProvider's filesystem watcher is enabled. When enabled, the watcher monitors the page directory for external changes and triggers cache invalidation. |
| `wikantik.cache.watcherInterval` | `int` | `3` | `wikantik_cache_watcherInterval` | How often (in seconds) the filesystem watcher polls for external changes. |
| `wikantik.cache.config-file` | `path` | *(blank: the bundled ehcache-wikantik.xml is used.)* | `wikantik_cache_config-file` | Classpath location of the Ehcache XML configuration (bundled at /ehcache-wikantik.xml inside wikantik-cache.jar). Override to ship a custom cache configuration on the classpath instead. A missing resource falls back to an in-code default cache set with no persistence tuning. |
| `wikantik.watcher.internalSaveGuardMillis` | `long` | `5000` | `wikantik_watcher_internalSaveGuardMillis` | Self-modification guard window (in milliseconds). Pages saved through Wikantik's own API are suppressed in the filesystem watcher for this duration, to avoid double-processing a save as an external change. |
| `wikantik.cache.memcached.servers` | `list` | *(blank: memcached adapter disabled (EhCache is the default).)* | `wikantik_cache_memcached_servers` | Comma-separated host:port list of memcached servers. Only consulted when the opt-in wikantik-cache-memcached module is wired in (see its Javadoc); the default CachingManager is EhCache and never reads this key. |
| `wikantik.cache.memcached.ttl` | `int` | `86400` | `wikantik_cache_memcached_ttl` | TTL, in seconds, for entries written by the memcached adapter. |
| `wikantik.cache.memcached.max-entries` | `int` | `1000` | `wikantik_cache_memcached_max-entries` | Reported max-entries for the memcached adapter's CacheInfo (a display value only - memcached itself has no per-cache entry cap, so this does not enforce one). |
| `wikantik.workDir` | `path` | *(blank: the ServletContext's temporary directory, or java.io.tmpdir)* | `wikantik_workDir` | The Wikantik working directory.  If not set, a temporary path will be used.  You can see the location of the workdir in the logs. It is HIGHLY recommended that you set this. The working directory is used to cache things like Lucene search results. if that is unavailable. |

## Attachments

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.attachment.provider` | `class` | `BasicAttachmentProvider` | `wikantik_attachment_provider` | ATTACHMENTS: Use the following property to define which attachment provider you want to use.  You have basically two choices: * Set the value to BasicAttachmentProvider a simple, flat file versioning provider * Leave the value empty (or just comment the line out) the attachment functionality is disabled |
| `wikantik.attachmentProvider` | `class` | *(blank: deprecated alias unset; falls back to wikantik.attachment.provider above.)* | `wikantik_attachmentProvider` | This property supersedes the deprecated wikantik.attachmentProvider below. |
| `wikantik.basicAttachmentProvider.storageDir` | `path` | *(blank: a "wikantik-files" directory in the user's home folder.)* | `wikantik_basicAttachmentProvider_storageDir` | The BasicAttachmentProvider needs to know where to store the files the user has uploaded.  It's okay to put these in the same directory as you put your text files (i.e. the pageDir setting above). If you're using Windows, then you must duplicate the backslashes. For example, use: Example: wikantik.basicAttachmentProvider.storageDir = C:\\Data\\jspwiki |
| `wikantik.basicAttachmentProvider.disableCache` | `string` | *(blank: no filename pattern is excluded; browser caching is enabled)* | `wikantik_basicAttachmentProvider_disableCache` | You can tell the BasicAttachmentProvider to add a flag so that browsers do not cache certain (or all) attachment types. This is useful in intranet environments. You should activate this if your users complain that their excel files are not uploaded correctly and they still do have an old version: Usually the file was uploaded correctly, but they get the locally cached version You can use regular expressions to disable the cache, e.g the following example will disable browser cache for all excel and word files: Example: wikantik.basicAttachmentProvider.disableCache = .*\.xls\|.*\.doc for all attachments. |
| `wikantik.attachment.maxsize` | `int` | *(blank: no limit (attachments up to Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes are accepted).)* | `wikantik_attachment_maxsize` | You can limit the maximum size of an attachment by setting this value.  The value is in bytes. This limit is not enforced for users with AdminPermissions. Example: the following would limit the attachment size to 100,000 bytes Example: wikantik.attachment.maxsize = 100000 |
| `wikantik.attachment.allowed` | `list` | *(blank: all attachment file types are allowed (no restriction).)* | `wikantik_attachment_allowed` | By default, Wikantik accepts all types of attachments.  However, you can allow some types only, or forbid some other types.  By default, all file types are allowed (if you do not specify the "allow" list at all, or it is empty). These allow/forbid statements are not enforced for users with AdminPermissions. These both are space-separated lists of file suffixes Example: Allow only PNG, JPG, ZIP and JAR file attachments Example: wikantik.attachment.allowed=.png .jpg .zip .jar |
| `wikantik.attachment.forbidden` | `list` | *(blank: no attachment file type is forbidden (subject to wikantik.attachment.allowed above).)* | `wikantik_attachment_forbidden` | Example: Forbid HTML, PHP, ASP and EXE Example: wikantik.attachment.forbidden = .html .htm .php .asp .exe |
| `wikantik.attachment.forceDownload` | `list` | `.html .htm .js .pdf .svg .xml` | `wikantik_attachment_forceDownload` | Attachment links to HTML, HTM and JS, etc. files will force a download rather than opening the attachment. Set to * to always enforce attachment download (or blank to force-download nothing). Space-separated list of file suffixes. |

The following choices are available: * TraditionalDiffProvider - Uses internal (java) diff to create a list of changes and shows it line by line colored. This is the default * ContextualDiffProvider - Uses internal (java) diff to create changes inline and shows it on a word by word basis using CSS. ## Encoding

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.encoding` | `enum(ISO-8859-1\|UTF-8)` | `UTF-8` | `wikantik_encoding` | Determines which character encoding Wikantik should use.  If you want to support all languages in your Wiki, you probably want to enable this.  From Wikantik 2.2, it is strongly suggested that you use UTF-8. Note that you can't switch these in the meantime, since the way the files are encoded on disk is incompatible between ISO-Latin1 and UTF-8. Don't try.  You'll get all sorts of interesting problems, if you do. Possible values are 'ISO-8859-1' and 'UTF-8' (default, if none has been specified). |

## Rendering & wiki syntax

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.breakTitleWithSpaces` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_breakTitleWithSpaces` | Usability niceties. If this property is set to "true", then page titles are rendered using an extra space between every capital letter.  It may make page titles readable on some occasions, but it does have the drawback of making the titles look a bit funny at times. |
| `wikantik.translatorReader.matchEnglishPlurals` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_translatorReader_matchEnglishPlurals` | If set to true, this property means that "WikiName" and "WikiNames" are considered equal when linking between them.  Setting this to true does not prevent you from having both kinds of pages - we just fall back to the other one if the primary name does not exist. For any other language, you'll probably want to turn this off. |
| `wikantik.translatorReader.camelCaseLinks` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_translatorReader_camelCaseLinks` | If you set this to true, the Wiki translator will then also consider "traditional" WikiNames (that is, names of pages JustSmashedTogether without square brackets) as hyperlinks.  This technique is also known as "CamelCase", or "BumpyCase", or "InterCapping".  I personally like CamelCase as a word, which is why this property is named as it is :-). By default, this is false, since traditional WikiLinks may confuse newbies. This option can be overridden on a per-page basis using the SET directive. |
| `wikantik.frontPage` | `string` | `Main` | `wikantik_frontPage` | The name of the front page.  This is the page that gets loaded if no other page is loaded.  Up until Wikantik 1.9.28, it was always called "Main", but now you can easily change the default front page here. |
| `wikantik.allowCreationOfEmptyPages` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_allowCreationOfEmptyPages` | Allow creation of empty pages. |
| `wikantik.translatorReader.useRelNofollow` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_translatorReader_useRelNofollow` | If set to "true", all external links are tagged with 'rel="nofollow"'. |
| `wikantik.translatorReader.useOutlinkImage` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_translatorReader_useOutlinkImage` | If set to true, all outward links have a small icon attached.  The icon can be found from images/out.png.  Default is true. |

| `wikantik.renderingManager.renderer` | `class` | `com.wikantik.render.markdown.MarkdownRenderer` | `wikantik_renderingManager_renderer` | Wiki renderer that outputs XHTML; it must be a subclass of com.wikantik.render.WikiRenderer |

## Search & hybrid retrieval

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.searchProvider` | `class` | `LuceneSearchProvider` | `wikantik_searchProvider` | Search provider used for searching pages and attachments. |
| `wikantik.lucene.analyzer` | `class` | `org.apache.lucene.analysis.standard.ClassicAnalyzer` | `wikantik_lucene_analyzer` | If your wiki's language is something else than English, you might want to visit lucene.apache.org and download a proper Analyzer for your language. |
| `wikantik.lucene.indexdelay` | `int` | `5` | `wikantik_lucene_indexdelay` | Lucene background updater timing (LuceneSearchProvider.LuceneUpdater). Seconds the updater thread sleeps between drains of the pending-page update queue - the steady-state cadence at which saved pages become searchable. |
| `wikantik.lucene.initialdelay` | `int` | `60` | `wikantik_lucene_initialdelay` | Seconds the updater waits after startup before its first pass, so the rest of engine startup settles before the index is touched. |
| `wikantik.lucene.missingPageCheckInterval` | `int` | `300` | `wikantik_lucene_missingPageCheckInterval` | How often, in seconds, the updater checks for pages that exist on disk but are missing from the index (a self-healing sweep). 0 disables the periodic check. |
| `wikantik.search.highlighter.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_search_highlighter_enabled` | Whether Lucene search results carry a highlighted excerpt (a fragment around the matching terms) via DefaultLuceneSearcher's Highlighter. Off by default; the current UI does not render the highlighted snippet, so this only matters for direct three-arg findPages(query, FLAG_CONTEXTS, ctx) callers. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.timeout-ms` | `long` | `2000` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_timeout-ms` | Hybrid retrieval query-time embedder (QueryEmbedderConfig). Wraps the embedding backend with a timeout, an in-memory Caffeine cache, a circuit breaker, and per-call metrics. Every user search calls the embedder; these knobs bound how much damage a flaky backend can cause. Values below are the QueryEmbedderConfig DEFAULT_* constants. Per-call embed timeout, in milliseconds. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.cache.ttl-seconds` | `long` | `14400` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_cache_ttl-seconds` | TTL for a cached query vector, in seconds. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.cache.max-entries` | `long` | `1000` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_cache_max-entries` | Caffeine cache maximum size (distinct cached query vectors). |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.breaker.window-size` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_breaker_window-size` | Rolling window of recent calls the circuit breaker uses to evaluate the failure rate. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.breaker.min-calls` | `int` | `10` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_breaker_min-calls` | Minimum observations in the window before the breaker will consider opening. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.breaker.failure-rate` | `double` | `0.5` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_breaker_failure-rate` | Failure rate (0.0-1.0) that trips the breaker open. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.embedder.breaker.cooldown-ms` | `long` | `30000` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_embedder_breaker_cooldown-ms` | How long the breaker stays OPEN before a probe is allowed, in milliseconds. |
| `wikantik.chunker.max_tokens` | `int` | `512` | `wikantik_chunker_max_tokens` | Hard ceiling on a non-atomic chunk's size, in estimated tokens (1 token ~= 4 chars). Oversized atomic blocks (fenced code, tables, short lists) pass through intact; oversized paragraphs fall back to sentence-level splitting to keep the embedder's context-window headroom. |
| `wikantik.chunker.merge_forward_tokens` | `int` | `150` | `wikantik_chunker_merge_forward_tokens` | Effective floor for chunk emission. A section's accumulated text below this threshold is held and merged forward into the next section (heading boundaries included), so short sibling sections coalesce into a single chunk of reasonable size. Default 150 tokens; raise to 200-300 for even coarser chunks (fewer extraction RPCs) at the cost of slightly diffuser embeddings on dense retrieval. Lower toward 50 to get more, smaller chunks with sharper per-chunk topicality. Note: changing this value shifts chunk boundaries, which changes content_hash and invalidates every row in kg_content_chunks, content_chunk_embeddings, and chunk_entity_mentions. Trigger a full content rebuild after editing. |
| `wikantik.chunker.fragment_floor_tokens` | `int` | `24` | `wikantik_chunker_fragment_floor_tokens` | Cross-section fragment floor (tokens). A section whose whole text is below this is a "fragment": it merges forward into the next section and adopts that section's heading_path, instead of becoming its own tiny, low-signal chunk. Sections at/above the floor always stand alone under their own heading (so they stay findable and their citations are correctly anchored). Must be <= merge_forward_tokens. 0 disables the floor (every section stands alone). Changing this invalidates chunk content - trigger a full content rebuild after editing. |
| `wikantik.chunker.overlap_tokens` | `int` | `40` | `wikantik_chunker_overlap_tokens` | Sliding-window overlap (tokens). After chunking, each chunk's tail is prepended to the next chunk under the same heading_path, so a fact straddling a chunk boundary appears whole in at least one chunk. 0 disables overlap. The 2026-06-14 probe showed a small @5/@20 recall gain. Changing this invalidates chunk content - full rebuild after. |
| `wikantik.chunker.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_chunker_enabled` | Kill-switch for save-time chunking. Disable if a chunker bug is blocking page saves (ChunkProjector is failure-isolated, but this lets ops short out the code path entirely). |
| `wikantik.rebuild.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_rebuild_enabled` | Kill-switch for the async post-save rebuild that drains Lucene writes and chunk re-projection after a page save. |
| `wikantik.rebuild.lucene_drain_poll_ms` | `int` | `2000` | `wikantik_rebuild_lucene_drain_poll_ms` | Poll interval, in milliseconds, while waiting for the Lucene writer queue to drain. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_enabled` | Master flag for the hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval path. When true (the default), /api/search fuses BM25 with dense embedding results. Fails closed to BM25-only if the embedding backend is unreachable or the query embedder circuit trips, so search stays usable regardless. Set to false to disable the dense path entirely (no embedding client is built and no bootstrap is scheduled). |
| `wikantik.search.ontologyExpansion.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_search_ontologyExpansion_enabled` | Whether the ontology-aware query expansion joins hybrid retrieval: when true, a query is expanded via the materialized RDF ontology (broader/ narrower/related terms) before search, if the ontology model is available. Default off (no expansion) - falls back to plain retrieval whenever the ontology is disabled or not yet built. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.page-aggregation` | `enum(max\|mean_top_3\|sum_top_3\|sum_top_5)` | `sum_top_3` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_page-aggregation` | How a page's per-chunk cosine scores collapse into one page-level score. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.rrf.k` | `int` | `60` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_rrf_k` | Reciprocal-rank-fusion constant for combining BM25 and dense page rankings. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.rrf.bm25-weight` | `double` | `1.0` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_rrf_bm25-weight` | BM25 side weight in the page-level RRF fusion. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.rrf.dense-weight` | `double` | `1.5` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_rrf_dense-weight` | Dense side weight in the page-level RRF fusion. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.rrf.truncate` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_rrf_truncate` | Number of fused page candidates kept after RRF, before returning results. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.dense.chunk-top` | `int` | `500` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_dense_chunk-top` | Chunk fan-out considered per query on the dense side before page aggregation. |
| `wikantik.search.hybrid.dense.page-top` | `int` | `100` | `wikantik_search_hybrid_dense_page-top` | Page candidates kept from the dense side after aggregation, before fusion. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.backend` | `enum(ollama)` | `ollama` | `wikantik_search_embedding_backend` | Which backend implementation to use. Currently supported: ollama. The client abstraction leaves room for future backends (e.g. Hugging Face TEI, OpenAI-compatible) - swapping is a config change, not a code change at call sites. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.base-url` | `url` | `http://inference.jakefear.com:11434` | `wikantik_search_embedding_base-url` | Root URL of the embedding server. Defaults to the dedicated inference host at inference.jakefear.com:11434. Override to http://localhost:11434 if you are running Ollama on the same box as the wiki. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.api-key` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_search_embedding_api-key` | Optional bearer token, forwarded as `Authorization: Bearer <value>`. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.model` | `string` | `qwen3-embedding-0.6b` | `wikantik_search_embedding_model` | Which candidate model to load. The wiki currently experiments with three options, each with its own prefix/dimension characteristics: nomic-embed-v1.5        - dim 768, asymmetric prefixes, Matryoshka bge-m3                  - dim 1024, no prefix, dense + sparse capable qwen3-embedding-0.6b    - dim 1024, Qwen3 instruction prompt on queries |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.ollama-tag` | `string` | *(blank: use EmbeddingModel.defaultOllamaTag() for the selected model.)* | `wikantik_search_embedding_ollama-tag` | Optional override of the default Ollama model tag for the selected model - useful when a deployment has pulled a non-default quantization or Modelfile variant (e.g. `bge-m3:latest`, or a custom Qwen3 tag). |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.timeout-ms` | `int` | `30000` | `wikantik_search_embedding_timeout-ms` | Per-request HTTP timeout in milliseconds. CPU-only backends on the mini-PC reference class can take 100+ ms per document at batch 32 - keep this well above the expected tail latency. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.batch-size` | `int` | `32` | `wikantik_search_embedding_batch-size` | Maximum number of texts sent per backend round-trip. Larger batches amortize model-load overhead on first call and improve throughput on a warm GPU; smaller batches reduce tail latency on CPU backends. |
| `wikantik.search.embedding.commit-batch-size` | `int` | `256` | `wikantik_search_embedding_commit-batch-size` | Rows committed per transaction during a corpus backfill. A full backfill is hours of inference on a CPU embedder; committing only at the end means any interruption (crash, restart, redeploy) discards every embedded row. This bounds that loss to one commit window. Sized against inference cost, not commit cost - a commit is sub-millisecond next to seconds-per-chunk embedding, so there is no throughput reason to raise it. Must be > 0. |
| `wikantik.search.dense.backend` | `enum(lucene-hnsw\|pgvector\|inmemory)` | `lucene-hnsw` | `wikantik_search_dense_backend` | Dense retrieval backend on the production wiring path (SearchWiringHelper. resolveDenseBackend), used whenever a DataSource is wired. One of: lucene-hnsw  - in-process Lucene HNSW ANN index (RAM), rebuilt on boot from content_chunk_embeddings; incremental upserts on save. Default (this is the docker1 production default). pgvector     - pgvector HNSW lookup against content_chunk_embeddings.embedding. Requires V032 + the one-shot backfill at bin/db/one-shots/2026-05-20-backfill-chunk-embeddings.sh. inmemory     - brute-force float[] scan. O(corpus) per query and per save; dev/small-corpus fallback only. Deliberately diverges from SearchSubsystemFactory.resolveFallbackDenseBackend, which defaults to 'inmemory' on the no-DataSource fallback path (the only backend that needs no DataSource) - do not "fix" the two to match; both defaults are pinned by DenseBackendResolutionTest. |
| `wikantik.search.dense.pgvector.ef_search` | `int` | `100` | `wikantik_search_dense_pgvector_ef_search` | pgvector HNSW ef_search recall/latency knob. Higher = better recall, more CPU. Default 100 is the design-doc baseline; 200-400 trade latency for recall on corpora where the parity smoke gate drifts. |
| `wikantik.search.dense.lucene.m` | `int` | `16` | `wikantik_search_dense_lucene_m` | Lucene HNSW dense backend (wikantik.search.dense.backend=lucene-hnsw). In-process approximate nearest-neighbour index held in RAM, rebuilt on boot from content_chunk_embeddings. Defaults match the pgvector HNSW index (HnswParams). |
| `wikantik.search.dense.lucene.ef_construction` | `int` | `64` | `wikantik_search_dense_lucene_ef_construction` | HNSW graph build-time candidate list size. Higher = better graph quality, slower builds. |
| `wikantik.search.dense.lucene.ef_search` | `int` | `100` | `wikantik_search_dense_lucene_ef_search` | HNSW query-time candidate list size. Higher = better recall, more CPU per query. |
| `wikantik.search.lucene.directory.kind` | `enum(nio\|mmap)` | `nio` | `wikantik_search_lucene_directory_kind` | How Lucene reads its on-disk index files. One of: nio   - NIOFSDirectory: per-read FileChannel.read() + buffer copy. Conservative default; matches all pre-flag deploys. mmap  - MMapDirectory: maps index files into virtual memory; reads served by the OS page cache as memory accesses. Lucene's recommended default on 64-bit Linux. A corrupt index page surfaces as SIGBUS instead of IOException - more visible failure mode. Read once at provider init; identical across read and write paths. |

| `wikantik.specialPage.EditProfile` | `string` | `preferences` | `wikantik_specialPage_EditProfile` | Serves profile editing. Currently routed through the preferences page. |
| `wikantik.specialPage.Preferences` | `string` | `preferences` | `wikantik_specialPage_Preferences` | Alias for UserPreferences. |
| `wikantik.specialPage.FindPage` | `string` | `search` | `wikantik_specialPage_FindPage` | Alias for Search. |
| `wikantik.urlConstructor` | `enum(DefaultURLConstructor\|ShortURLConstructor\|ShortViewURLConstructor)` | `ShortViewURLConstructor` | `wikantik_urlConstructor` | URL Constructor Wikantik by default generates page and attachment links that use JSP pages and request parameters. It can also use alternative URL constructors so that URL pages resemble traditional website paths, too. You have three choices for generating URLs: DefaultURLConstructor - uses JSPs for all references: http://mywiki.com/wikantik/Wiki.jsp?page=Main http://mywiki.com/wikantik/Edit.jsp?page=Main ShortURLConstructor - uses path-like reference style: http://mywiki.com/wikantik/wiki/Main http://mywiki.com/wikantik/wiki/Main?do=Edit ShortViewURLConstructor - uses path-like references for views; JSPs for everything else: http://mywiki.com/wikantik/wiki/Main http://mywiki.com/wikantik/Edit.jsp?page=Main Of course, you can also write your own implementation if you wish. For either of the ShortURL constructors, you can also specify a prefix path to go in front of page names. By default, the prefix is 'wiki/'. Be warned that the ShortURLConstructor does not work well with any other editor except the built-in plaintext one.  Use ShortViewURLConstructor if you plan to enable any other ones. e.g. DefaultURLConstructor. |
| `wikantik.shortURLConstructor.prefix` | `string` | `wiki/` | `wikantik_shortURLConstructor_prefix` | This prefix must be in some elements of web.xml, too: in servlet-mapping of WikiServlet, in filter-mapping of WikiJSPFilter |

## Plugins

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.plugin.searchPath` | `list` | *(blank: no extra package added; only the built-in com.wikantik.plugin path is searched.)* | `wikantik_plugin_searchPath` | Plugin search paths. Define here the packages you want to use for searching plugins, separated with commas. For example, use this to add "org.myorganisation.wikantik.myplugins" and "com.foobar.myplugins" to the search path (comma-separated). The default path is "com.wikantik.plugin", and it will be always the last item on the path.  This allows you to override Wikantik default plugins.  Note that you are only adding to the path, not replacing it (ie. the default path is never removed.) If the path is not specified (and there is no jspwiki_module.xml with the plugin JAR), you need to either declare the search path by hand, or use a fully qualified name. If you are a plugin developer, please consider deploying a jspwiki_module.xml file with your plugin JAR, so that the user does not have to set the searchPath. e.g. wikantik.plugin.searchPath = org.myorganisation.wikantik.myplugins,com.foobar.myplugins Comma-separated list of package names. |
| `wikantik.plugin.externalJars` | `list` | *(blank: no extra jars are added to the plugin classpath.)* | `wikantik_plugin_externalJars` | You can specify external jars containing plugin classes. These will be added to the classpath when plugins are loaded. Using this you don't have to put the jars in your WEB-INF/lib directory thereby preventing war-surgery. Comma-separated list of jar paths. |

## Authentication

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.loginModule.class` | `class` | `com.wikantik.auth.login.UserDatabaseLoginModule` | `wikantik_loginModule_class` | Wikantik supports a plugin-based interface for talking to different kinds of authentication and authorization systems. By "authentication," we mean a system for logging in a user to establish their identity. By "authorization," we mean a system for figuring out what actions users can perform based on their authenticated identities. For users looking to get started quickly, the default settings below should work fine. In addition to the properties below, you may also want to modify the security policy file WEB-INF/wikantik.policy. See the policy file for more details. AUTHENTICATION For authentication, Wikantik uses JAAS (Java Authentication and Authorization Service) in combination with a servlet filter that picks up any credentials set by the servlet container. The Authentication system is configured below. You must choose either (A) Container or (B) Custom authentication. (B) is the default. A) CONTAINER AUTHENTICATION Wikantik will always (passively) collect credentials supplied by your servlet container, via HttpServletRequest.getUserPrincipal/getRemote user. You do not need to do anything to enable this. In addition, you can cause Wikantik users to log in to the web container by uncommenting the the <security-constraint> elements in WEB-INF/web.xml. B) CUSTOM AUTHENTICATION If you do not wish to use container-managed authentication, you can use Wikantik's own custom authentication system. This uses a JAAS LoginModule (supplied below) to log in the user. You can use any JAAS LoginModule you want. The default class is com.wikantik.auth.login.UserDatabaseLoginModule, which compares the supplied username and hashed password with the values stored in the configured UserDatabase (see USER DATABASE below). Supply the JAAS LoginModule class used for custom authentication here. The implementation MUST have a zero-argument constructor (as noted in the javax.security.auth.spi.LoginModule Javadocs). |
| `wikantik.login.throttling` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_login_throttling` | Login Throttling - Whether logins should be throttled to limit bruce-force attempts. |

## Security & passwords

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.auth.masterpassword` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_auth_masterpassword` | Wiki-variable name for a legacy master-password override. DefaultVariableManager unconditionally blocks this exact name from ever resolving through the [{$var}] wiki-variable syntax (THE_BIG_NO_NO_LIST), regardless of whether a value is set here - so a value in this file would never be exposed to page markup either way. Kept blank; nothing in this codebase otherwise reads this key. |
| `wikantik.auth.password.verifyCache.ttlSeconds` | `long` | *(blank: 60 seconds (the built-in default).)* | `-Dwikantik.auth.password.verifyCache.ttlSeconds` only | TTL, in seconds, of the short-lived cache of successful bcrypt password verifications (AbstractUserDatabase). Speeds up stateless HTTP Basic clients (monitoring pollers, cron jobs, CI scripts) that resend credentials on every request and would otherwise pay a full ~150-250ms bcrypt key-stretch each time. A value <= 0 disables the cache entirely. Read via System.getProperty, not from this file - set it as a JVM system property (-Dwikantik.auth.password.verifyCache.ttlSeconds=...). |
| `wikantik.password.minLength` | `int` | `8` | `wikantik_password_minLength` | Minimum acceptable password length (NIST 800-63B: length over complexity rules). |
| `wikantik.password.maxLength` | `int` | `128` | `wikantik_password_maxLength` | Maximum acceptable password length. |
| `wikantik.password.blocklist.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_password_blocklist_enabled` | Whether new/changed passwords are checked against a bundled common-passwords blocklist and rejected if found. |
| `wikantik.plugin.jdbc.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_plugin_jdbc_enabled` | Kill switch for JDBCPlugin, which executes page-authored SQL (via [{JDBC ...}]) against the wiki's own datasource using the high-privilege application DB role. Ships disabled: enabling it means any editor with edit permission on a page can run arbitrary SQL as that role. Turn it on only if you accept that exposure, and pair it with the plugin's own admin-permission check. |
| `wikantik.admin.bootstrap` | `string` | *(blank: no bootstrap admin override is active.)* | `wikantik_admin_bootstrap` | Bootstrap admin override: the named user bypasses all policy checks (gets AllPermission) for wikantik.admin.bootstrap.maxAgeSeconds after startup. Intended only for recovering access to a fresh or locked-out installation; remove this property once a real admin account is confirmed working. |
| `wikantik.admin.bootstrap.maxAgeSeconds` | `long` | *(blank: 86400 seconds (24 hours).)* | `wikantik_admin_bootstrap_maxAgeSeconds` | Lifetime, in seconds, of the wikantik.admin.bootstrap override, starting at server startup. |

## Cookies & sessions

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.cookieAssertions` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_cookieAssertions` | Cookie authentication & assertion If this value is set to "true", then Wikantik will allow you to "assert" an identity using a cookie.  It's still considered to be unsafe, just like no login at all, but it is useful when you have no need to force everyone to login. By default, this is on. |
| `wikantik.cookieAuthentication` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_cookieAuthentication` | If you would like to keep your users logged in for weeks at a time, you can turn on "cookie authentication" feature.  However, this comes with important security caveats: 1) User will stay logged in into your system for weeks.  This means that if someone manages to nab the cookie during this time, they can pretend to be that user. 2) The mappings between cookies and users are written in your filesystem, in $wikantik.workDir/logincookies.  Access to this directory means that the ability to fake anyone in the wiki, so please make sure that only the proper admin has read access to this directory. When enabled, a successful password login also issues a remember-me cookie (WikantikUID): httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure when the request is HTTPS, and an opaque server-validated token (not a forgeable credential). Because it is Lax, a later request silently re-authenticates after the server session is gone (Tomcat restart/redeploy, session timeout) instead of bouncing the user to the login screen - recommended to avoid surprise logouts on deploy. Logout clears it. SSO users are unaffected (they re-auth via the IdP session). By default, cookie authentication is off; set to true to enable remember-me. |
| `wikantik.cookieAuthentication.expiry` | `int` | `14` | `wikantik_cookieAuthentication_expiry` | Defines how many days the cookies are kept, and how often the people have to log in. The default is two weeks, i.e. 14 days.  If you need a shorter period than one day, turn off cookie authentication, then tweak your web.xml to allow for longer sessions. |

## SSO

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.sso.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_sso_enabled` | SINGLE SIGN-ON (SSO) Wikantik supports enterprise Single Sign-On via OIDC (OpenID Connect) and SAML 2.0 protocols using the pac4j library. This allows users to authenticate with external Identity Providers such as Azure AD, Okta, Google Workspace, Keycloak, PingFederate, ADFS, and others. To enable SSO, set wikantik.sso.enabled=true and configure the appropriate protocol settings below. When SSO is enabled, a "Login with SSO" button will appear on the login page. All wikantik.sso.* properties below are read directly from this file (not bridged through JAAS LoginModule options), so leaving them at their shipped blank/default values keeps SSO fully off regardless of what else is set - only wikantik.sso.enabled turns it on. |
| `wikantik.sso.type` | `enum(oidc\|saml\|both)` | `oidc` | `wikantik_sso_type` | SSO type: "oidc" for OpenID Connect, "saml" for SAML 2.0, or "both". |
| `wikantik.sso.oidc.discoveryUri` | `url` | *(blank: OIDC is not configured; if SSO is enabled with an oidc/both type,)* | `wikantik_sso_oidc_discoveryUri` | Required when wikantik.sso.type = oidc or both. The OIDC discovery URI (/.well-known/openid-configuration endpoint). no OIDC client is built and an error is logged (SSO falls back to any configured SAML client, or to no SSO at all). |
| `wikantik.sso.oidc.clientId` | `string` | *(blank: OIDC is not configured (see wikantik.sso.oidc.discoveryUri).)* | `wikantik_sso_oidc_clientId` | The OAuth 2.0 client ID issued by your Identity Provider. |
| `wikantik.sso.oidc.clientSecret` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_sso_oidc_clientSecret` | The OAuth 2.0 client secret issued by your Identity Provider. Never commit a real value to version control; set it via wikantik-custom.properties instead. |
| `wikantik.sso.oidc.scope` | `string` | `openid profile email` | `wikantik_sso_oidc_scope` | The OIDC scopes to request. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.identityProviderMetadataPath` | `path` | *(blank: SAML is not configured; if SSO is enabled with a saml/both type,)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_identityProviderMetadataPath` | Required when wikantik.sso.type = saml or both. Path to the Identity Provider's SAML metadata XML file. no SAML client is built and an error is logged. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.serviceProviderEntityId` | `string` | *(blank: SAML is not configured (see wikantik.sso.saml.identityProviderMetadataPath).)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_serviceProviderEntityId` | The Service Provider entity ID (usually the wiki's URL). |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.keystorePath` | `path` | *(blank: no keystore is configured; SAML assertion signing/encryption that)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_keystorePath` | Path to the SAML keystore (for signing/encryption). needs one will fail if SAML is otherwise enabled. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.keystorePassword` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_keystorePassword` | Keystore password. Never commit a real value to version control; set it via wikantik-custom.properties instead. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.privateKeyPassword` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_privateKeyPassword` | Private key password. Never commit a real value to version control; set it via wikantik-custom.properties instead. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.authnRequestBindingType` | `string` | *(blank: pac4j's own default binding is used (no explicit override).)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_authnRequestBindingType` | SAML AuthnRequest binding type. Controls which binding pac4j uses when sending the AuthnRequest to the IdP's SingleSignOnService; the value must match a binding the IdP advertises in its metadata. HTTP-Redirect (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect) is the supported and recommended binding - the SSORedirectServlet issues a 302 redirect carrying the AuthnRequest as a query parameter. HTTP-POST AuthnRequest is not supported by the current redirect servlet; do not set the HTTP-POST binding here unless the redirect servlet is extended to render form-post content. |
| `wikantik.sso.saml.serviceProviderMetadataPath` | `path` | *(blank: pac4j keeps the SP metadata in memory only (not persisted to disk).)* | `wikantik_sso_saml_serviceProviderMetadataPath` | Optional path where pac4j writes the generated SP metadata XML file. When set, pac4j persists the SP's SPSSODescriptor (including the registered ACS URL) to this file and re-reads it on restart; without this, pac4j holds the SP metadata only in memory and may fail to resolve the ACS URL during assertion validation against some IdP implementations. |
| `wikantik.sso.autoProvision` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_sso_autoProvision` | When enabled, a local user profile is automatically created from IdP claims on first SSO login. |
| `wikantik.sso.identityClaim` | `string` | `sub` | `wikantik_sso_identityClaim` | IdP claim treated as the immutable identity used to link an SSO login to a local account (the account-link key). Set to "preferred_username" only if you trust your IdP to keep that claim stable and unique - it is mutable at most IdPs, unlike "sub". |

## Authorization

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.authorizer` | `class` | `com.wikantik.auth.authorize.WebContainerAuthorizer` | `wikantik_authorizer` | AUTHORIZATION For authorization, Wikantik has a two-tier system. When we want to determine whether a user has permission to perform a certain action, we first consult (A) an external "authorizer" to determine if the user is a member of the required role. In addition to checking its external authorizer, it also checks (B) its GroupManager for wiki-managed groups. A) EXTERNAL AUTHORIZATION By default, Wikantik uses the servlet container's authorization service for to check what roles the user belongs to (that is, it calls HttpServletRequest.isUserInRole(String)). After the user authenticates, the default Authorizer (WebContainerAuthorizer) checks to see if the user belongs to the roles listed in web.xml using <security-role>/<role-name> or <auth-constraint>/<role-name> elements. However, you can use another Authorizer if you wish; specify that class here. |
| `wikantik.policy.file` | `string` | *(blank: the built-in default policy file name, "wikantik.policy".)* | `wikantik_policy_file` | Security policy file name, resolved via Engine.findConfigFile (WEB-INF, then classpath). The database-backed policy_grants table is used whenever wikantik.datasource resolves, which is always in a supported deployment (see the Database section); this file is the legacy fallback for a deployment without a datasource and is otherwise never read. |
| `wikantik.groupdatabase` | `class` | `com.wikantik.auth.authorize.JDBCGroupDatabase` | `wikantik_groupdatabase` | B) GROUPS As an additional source of authorization, users can belong to discretionary "wiki groups" that the users manage themselves. Wiki groups are stored in a GroupDatabase. The default group database persists members in the configured JDBC datasource (see the JDBC section below). Override with your own GroupDatabase implementation with this property: |

Matching is by cluster path as declared on the page's hub, not by page name. |

Generate one at https://www.bing.com/indexnow and publish it at https://<your-host>/<key>.txt as IndexNow requires. "apiKey not configured" error; Google Sitemap Ping is unaffected. |

| `wikantik.page_ownership.default_owner` | `string` | `agents` | `wikantik_page_ownership_default_owner` | Login name of the fallback page owner recorded for agent-authored or otherwise unattributable page saves (see PageOwnerService / the "agents" service account). Stored at bootstrap only when it names a real user, so an unseeded value degrades safely to no owner rather than a dangling reference. |
| `wikantik.page_ownership.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_page_ownership_enforcement_enabled` | Master flag for PageOwnershipSaveFilter, which records a page_owners row on every save. Failures are logged and swallowed - ownership tracking never blocks a save - so disabling this only stops new rows from being written. |

| `wikantik.knowledge.extractor.claude.model` | `string` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `wikantik_knowledge_extractor_claude_model` | Anthropic model id used when backend=claude. claude-haiku-4-5 is the recommended default for cost; swap to claude-sonnet-4-6 for higher quality on ambiguous corpora. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the JVM environment. |

NOTE: KgJudgeConfig reads this same key, so the judge uses it too - decouple with a dedicated judge model key if the judge ever wants a different model. |

| `wikantik.knowledge.extractor.timeout_ms` | `int` | `120000` | `wikantik_knowledge_extractor_timeout_ms` | Per-chunk HTTP timeout. Self-hosted Ollama with multi-thousand-token prompts can need well over 30s; 120s is the shipping default so batch jobs don't time out on every chunk against smaller hardware. |
| `wikantik.knowledge.extractor.confidence_threshold` | `double` | `0.6` | `wikantik_knowledge_extractor_confidence_threshold` | Proposals below this confidence are dropped, not filed - keeps the proposal queue reviewable. |

| `wikantik.knowledge.extractor.per_page_min_interval_ms` | `int` | `5000` | `wikantik_knowledge_extractor_per_page_min_interval_ms` | Minimum interval between extraction runs for the same page, in ms. Protects the extractor from a re-save storm; set to 0 to disable. |
| `wikantik.knowledge.extractor.concurrency` | `int` | `2` | `wikantik_knowledge_extractor_concurrency` | Max parallel extraction RPCs fired by the admin batch job. Save-time extraction is always serial; this only affects /admin/knowledge/extract-mentions. Clamped to [1, 4] at load time. |
| `wikantik.genai.mode` | `enum(full\|embeddings-only\|none)` | `full` | `wikantik_genai_mode` | Limits what LLM operations are allowed. One of: full           - both embeddings and chat inference allowed (default / current behavior) embeddings-only - embeddings for retrieval/search enabled only; no chat inference none           - all LLM operations disabled An absent property means 'full' (silent - the normal state of existing deployments). A set-but-blank or unrecognized value also means 'full', with a logged warning, so operator typos and old deployments degrade gracefully. To enforce, watch the warn logs. |
| `wikantik.knowledge.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_knowledge_enabled` | When false, the Knowledge Graph feature set is not constructed at all: no KG services, no KG MCP tools (knowledge-mcp KG tools and admin-mcp KG curation tools are not registered), and /admin/knowledge-graph/* plus /api/page-knowledge/* return 503 naming this flag. Chunking and the embedding/dense-retrieval pipeline stay fully active - they are independent of the KG. Entity extraction is skipped regardless of wikantik.knowledge.extractor.backend. The ontology layer keeps its own flag (wikantik.ontology.enabled); with the KG off its entity projections no-op while page/cluster/tag concept graphs continue to work. |
| `wikantik.kg_policy.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_kg_policy_enabled` | Cluster-primary, page-overridable, admin-administered policy for which pages contribute to the knowledge graph. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-kg-inclusion-policy-design.md. Search remains governed by SystemPageRegistry.isSystemPage(); this layer only affects the KG. Master switch. Default true - wires the policy components into the engine at boot. Setting to false reverts to legacy behaviour (no exclusion). |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_kg_judge_enabled` | Knowledge Graph staged validation - judge LLM Async judge LLM that promotes extractor proposals into materialised kg_nodes/kg_edges at tier='machine'; admin approval upgrades to tier='human'. Read paths default to min_tier='machine' (broader view); callers can pass min_tier=human for the strict view. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.endpoint` | `url` | *(blank: falls back to wikantik.knowledge.extractor.ollama.base_url)* | `wikantik_kg_judge_endpoint` | When unset, judge connection falls back to the extractor's wikantik.knowledge.extractor.ollama.base_url (then .ollama.endpoint, then the host compiled into KgJudgeConfig.DEFAULT_ENDPOINT - a private inference host that a fresh deployment must override). Override only to pin the judge to a different endpoint than the extractor. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.model` | `string` | *(blank: falls back to wikantik.knowledge.extractor.ollama.model)* | `wikantik_kg_judge_model` | When unset, judge model falls back to the extractor's wikantik.knowledge.extractor.ollama.model (then KgJudgeConfig.DEFAULT_MODEL). Override only to pin the judge to a different model than the extractor. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.keep_alive` | `string` | `30m` | `wikantik_kg_judge_keep_alive` | How long Ollama keeps the judge model resident in memory between calls. Longer than the cron interval so the model stays loaded across batches - shorter values caused every cron pass to eat a cold-load on its first 1-2 proposals. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.cron.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_kg_judge_cron_enabled` | Whether the scheduled cron trigger runs the judge automatically. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.cron.interval_min` | `int` | `5` | `wikantik_kg_judge_cron_interval_min` | Minutes between scheduled judge runs. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.batch_size` | `int` | `50` | `wikantik_kg_judge_batch_size` | Maximum number of proposals processed per judge run. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.concurrency` | `int` | `2` | `wikantik_kg_judge_concurrency` | Number of proposals judged in parallel per run. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.timeout_seconds` | `int` | `120` | `wikantik_kg_judge_timeout_seconds` | Per-proposal judge LLM call timeout, in seconds. |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.max_attempts` | `int` | `3` | `wikantik_kg_judge_max_attempts` | Maximum retry attempts for a single proposal before it is marked failed. |
| `wikantik.kg.read.default_min_tier` | `enum(machine\|human)` | `machine` | `wikantik_kg_read_default_min_tier` | Default tier for read paths when caller does not pass min_tier. Set to 'human' to enforce strict-only view across the deployment. |
| `wikantik.kg.extractor.allow_claude` | `boolean` | `false` | `-Dwikantik.kg.extractor.allow_claude` only | Both flags gate the standalone extract-cli's optional Claude (Anthropic SDK) code paths ("--extractor claude" / "--judge claude" on BootstrapExtractionCli / JudgeExperimentCli); they are read only as JVM system properties (-Dwikantik.kg.extractor.allow_claude=true), never from this file - a value set here has no effect. The default (unset -> false) refuses the premium path even when an Anthropic key is available, so a stray CLI invocation never bills the paid tier by accident (ADR-0007). |
| `wikantik.kg.judge.allow_claude` | `boolean` | `false` | `-Dwikantik.kg.judge.allow_claude` only | Same cost guard as above, for the extract-cli's judge path ("--judge claude"). Read only as -Dwikantik.kg.judge.allow_claude=true. |
| `wikantik.citations.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_citations_enabled` | Parse cite:// body markup into the derived `citations` table, grade span-level staleness as the base churns, and surface stale citations (admin/drift, the list_stale_citations MCP tool, the for-agent projection). Requires a datasource; degrades to a no-op when absent. Set false to disable citation tracking entirely. |

## Ontology

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.ontology.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_ontology_enabled` | Master switch for the ontology layer (OntologyWiringHelper). When false, no TDB2 store is built and /sparql, /id/{type}/{id} and /export/*.{ttl,nt} return "ontology disabled". The Knowledge Graph and page/cluster/tag concept projections are unaffected - this flag only gates their RDF materialization. |
| `wikantik.ontology.tdb2.dir` | `path` | *(blank: <wikantik.workDir>/ontology-tdb2 (or java.io.tmpdir/wikantik-ontology-tdb2 when workDir is unset))* | `wikantik_ontology_tdb2_dir` | Directory for the Jena TDB2 store behind /sparql, /id/* and /export/*. The store is a rebuildable cache: deleting it and restarting triggers a full re-projection from PostgreSQL. |
| `wikantik.ontology.rebuild.interval.hours` | `long` | `24` | `wikantik_ontology_rebuild_interval_hours` | Hours between full nightly rebuilds of the TDB2 store from PostgreSQL - a reconciliation backstop that catches KG drift and any missed incremental sync events. 0 disables the scheduled rebuild entirely (incremental sync and the startup-if-empty self-heal still run). |
| `wikantik.ontology.compaction.interval.hours` | `long` | `168` | `wikantik_ontology_compaction_interval_hours` | Hours between periodic TDB2 compactions. The store's copy-on-write B+Trees never shrink on their own, so continuous rewriting (nightly rebuild + every incremental sync) only ever grows it - measured production growth is ~1.35 GB/day. Weekly is deliberately less aggressive than the daily rebuild interval; 0 disables scheduled compaction (same 0=disabled convention as the rebuild interval above). |
| `wikantik.ontology.incremental.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_ontology_incremental_enabled` | Event-incremental entity sync: re-project an entity's graph on KgChangeEvent (from both KG write funnels) instead of waiting for the nightly rebuild. When false, entity graphs are only refreshed by the nightly rebuild/backstop. |
| `wikantik.ontology.incremental.coalesce.ms` | `long` | `500` | `wikantik_ontology_incremental_coalesce_ms` | Coalescing window for incremental entity sync, in milliseconds - batches rapid-fire KgChangeEvents for the same entity into a single re-projection instead of re-projecting on every individual write. |

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |

Pages that already carry frontmatter, or that match the system-page predicate, are always left untouched. |
| `wikantik.frontmatter.defaultTags` | `int` | *(blank: no default tags are added (an explicit override to disable tag generation without disabling the rest of the auto-defaulting block; omitting the key entirely instead uses the built-in default of 3))* | `wikantik_frontmatter_defaultTags` | Number of keywords the auto-defaulting filter extracts into the generated tags: list (TagExtractor, log-dampened TF scoring). Only consulted when wikantik.frontmatter.autoDefaults is true. |
| `wikantik.frontmatter.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_frontmatter_enforcement_enabled` | Master flag for save-time frontmatter schema enforcement. ERROR violations (including malformed YAML) refuse the save; WARNING violations are stashed for the REST/MCP layer to surface on a successful response. Disable only while migrating an existing dirty corpus. |
| `wikantik.frontmatter.enum.nonCanonical.severity` | `enum(warning\|error)` | `warning` | `wikantik_frontmatter_enum_nonCanonical_severity` | Severity for a curated-open enum field (e.g. type, audience) holding a value outside its canonical set. 'warning' lets the save through with an advisory; 'error' refuses it. |
| `wikantik.frontmatter.trustedAuthors` | `list` | *(blank: the verified_by trust check is disabled - every author is)* | `wikantik_frontmatter_trustedAuthors` | Comma-separated list of author names/logins trusted for the verified_by advisory check. treated as trusted (no restriction) |
| `wikantik.structural_spine.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_structural_spine_enforcement_enabled` | Master flag for structural-spine enforcement: auto-assigns a fresh canonical_id to any page saved without one. Setting to false reverts to Phase 2 warn-only behaviour (no auto-assignment). |
| `wikantik.cluster_declaration.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_cluster_declaration_enforcement_enabled` | Gates the duplicate-cluster-declaration ERROR (ClusterDeclarationDesign Phase 2): two hub pages declaring the same cluster: path. Ships FALSE deliberately - both the repo and production corpora were verified clean of duplicate declarations at Phase 0, but flipping this on against a corpus that still has duplicates makes the offending hub pages un-saveable, trapping the very content that needs editing to fix them. Only enable after re-verifying the target corpus is clean (see ClusterDeclarationDesign.md). |
| `wikantik.runbook.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_runbook_enforcement_enabled` | Master flag for runbook frontmatter enforcement: when a page declares type: runbook, its runbook: block must satisfy the schema rules in FrontmatterRunbookValidator or the save is refused. Non-runbook pages are always unaffected. |
| `wikantik.math.enforcement.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_math_enforcement_enabled` | Master flag for save-time LaTeX validation of the page body. ERROR violations refuse the save (HTTP 422 / MCP refusal); WARNING violations are stashed for the REST/MCP layer to surface on a successful response. |

## Context bundle & briefing

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.briefing.log.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_briefing_log_enabled` | Whether real /api/briefing and get_briefing (MCP) requests are recorded to briefing_log for later analysis. Writes run on a single bounded-queue daemon thread that drops the oldest pending record when saturated under load, so a traffic spike never back-pressures briefing assembly. |
| `wikantik.bundle.coverage.strong_similarity` | `double` | `0.55` | `wikantik_bundle_coverage_strong_similarity` | A section's dense cosine similarity at/above this counts as "strong" coverage. |
| `wikantik.bundle.coverage.partial_similarity` | `double` | `0.40` | `wikantik_bundle_coverage_partial_similarity` | A section's dense cosine similarity at/above this (but below strong_similarity) counts as "partial" coverage; below it counts as no coverage. |
| `wikantik.bundle.reranker.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_bundle_reranker_enabled` | RAG-as-a-Service context-bundle reranker (GET /api/bundle, assemble_bundle MCP). Listwise section reranker over the per-page shortlist. DEFAULT OFF: the 2026-06-13 LIVE end-to-end measurement (eval/bundle-corpus/ baseline-notes.md) showed the listwise reranker is an ORDERING lever, not a recall lever - rerank recall == dense recall at the bundle's operating point - while adding ~1.5s/request. The bundle ships dense-ordered (already relevance- sorted) by default; flip 'enabled' to true to opt into reranked ordering. |
| `wikantik.bundle.reranker.model` | `string` | `gemma4:e4b` | `wikantik_bundle_reranker_model` | Ollama model used for reranking when enabled=true. gemma4:e4b (think:false) is the shipped latency/quality pick. |
| `wikantik.bundle.reranker.base_url` | `url` | `http://inference.jakefear.com:11434` | `wikantik_bundle_reranker_base_url` | Ollama base URL for the reranker model; only consulted when enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.reranker.timeout_ms` | `int` | `30000` | `wikantik_bundle_reranker_timeout_ms` | Per-call reranker HTTP timeout, in milliseconds; only consulted when enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.rerank.chain` | `string` | *(blank: identity chain - bundle behavior is byte-identical to pre-chain (falls back to the legacy wikantik.bundle.reranker.enabled flag above).)* | `wikantik_bundle_rerank_chain` | Ordered, comma-separated stage names applied after RRF fusion, before dedup/top-N. Stages: mmr (lexical MMR diversity), metadata-boost (confidence tie-breaker, see below), llm (listwise LLM reranker; overrides reranker.enabled). Enable only after a measured recall@12 no-regression run (see eval/bundle-corpus/baseline-notes.md). Example: wikantik.bundle.rerank.chain = mmr |
| `wikantik.bundle.rerank.mmr.lambda` | `double` | `0.7` | `wikantik_bundle_rerank_mmr_lambda` | MMR lambda: 1.0 = pure relevance (no diversity), 0.0 = pure diversity. |
| `wikantik.bundle.rerank.metadata_boost.positions` | `double` | `1.5` | `wikantik_bundle_rerank_metadata_boost_positions` | metadata-boost stage: bounded confidence rank tie-breaker (AUTHORITATIVE up, STALE down) that nudges a candidate by up to +/-positions rank slots relative to the upstream order. Composes with mmr/llm (it boosts incoming RANK, not denseScore). Active only when 'metadata-boost' is in the chain AND a confidence lookup is wired. positions = max rank shift (0 disables). NOTE: ranks are integers, so a value below ~0.5 never reorders anything (silent no-op) and AUTHORITATIVE-over-PROVISIONAL needs > 1; 1.5 is the useful floor for a genuine tie-breaker, higher = more aggressive shuffling. |
| `wikantik.bundle.rerank.metadata_boost.window` | `int` | `24` | `wikantik_bundle_rerank_metadata_boost_window` | Top-N candidates the metadata-boost stage may reorder. |
| `wikantik.bundle.eval.interval.hours` | `double` | `0` | `wikantik_bundle_eval_interval_hours` | Interval in hours between scheduled bundle-eval runs against eval/bundle-corpus. 0 = DISABLED (default) - a real run needs a live embedding index, so enable only in a deployment that has one. Each run persists recall@12 to bundle_eval_run and logs a regression WARN when any recall falls below its threshold floor (thresholds.properties). |
| `wikantik.bundle.eval.precision_k` | `int` | `12` | `wikantik_bundle_eval_precision_k` | Precision@K computed by each scheduled eval run. |
| `wikantik.bundle.eval.corpus` | `path` | `eval/bundle-corpus/queries.csv` | `wikantik_bundle_eval_corpus` | CSV of eval queries (query text + expected page/section) consulted by the scheduled eval run - only read when interval.hours > 0. |
| `wikantik.bundle.sections_per_page` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_bundle_sections_per_page` | Per-page section shortlist depth for the context bundle. Raised 5 -> 20 on 2026-06-14: once contextual embeddings made section scores discriminative, the cap of 5 became the binding constraint and discarded measured recall (realized bundle recall@12 0.602 -> 0.685 when loosened). The bundle still returns the top MAX_SECTIONS overall; this only controls how many per page enter the candidate pool. |
| `wikantik.bundle.dense.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_bundle_dense_enabled` | Bundle candidate source. Default true = retrieve the top-K chunks globally from the dense index (no page pre-select), group to sections. The 2026-06-14 measurement showed this realises the section-recall ceiling (recall@12 0.735) where the page-gated hybrid path only reaches ~0.685 (the page pre-select drops retrievable sections). Set false to fall back to the page-gated path. |
| `wikantik.bundle.dense.top_k` | `int` | `300` | `wikantik_bundle_dense_top_k` | Bounds the global chunk fan-out when dense.enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.knee.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_bundle_knee_enabled` | Knee cutoff: dynamic-N - return fewer, denser sections when dense relevance falls off a cliff, instead of always padding to the top-N. |
| `wikantik.bundle.knee.retain_ratio` | `double` | `0.5` | `wikantik_bundle_knee_retain_ratio` | retain_ratio keeps sections whose dense score is >= retain_ratio x the top score (0.5 = at least half as strong as the best). Only consulted when knee.enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_enabled` | Chunk-level BM25 hybrid bundle source (default ON since 2026-06-18). Wraps the dense chunk source with a RAM Lucene BM25 chunk index + RRF fusion (the lexical half of "hybrid" at chunk granularity). The sweep found a STRICT improvement over dense-only with the tuned defaults below: similarity recall@12 0.711->0.737, overall 0.706->0.721, NO category regresses. Costs a second in-RAM index (~18.4k chunks, a few MB) built at startup; degrades to dense-only if that build fails. Set false to revert. See eval/bm25-chunk-spike/findings.md. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.bm25_weight` | `double` | `0.5` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_bm25_weight` | Bundle fusion weights (separate from the page-level wikantik.search.hybrid.rrf.* knobs). Tuned 2026-06-18: half the page-level BM25 weight + a tighter rrfK keep the similarity gain without the boundary@5 dip that the reused page weights (bm25=1.0) caused. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.dense_weight` | `double` | `1.5` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_dense_weight` | Dense-score fusion weight, paired with bm25_weight above. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.rrf_k` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_rrf_k` | RRF fusion k constant for combining BM25 and dense chunk rankings. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.truncate` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_truncate` | Number of fused chunk candidates kept before grouping to sections. |
| `wikantik.bundle.bm25.analyzer` | `enum(standard\|code)` | `standard` | `wikantik_bundle_bm25_analyzer` | BM25 chunk-index analyzer: standard \| code. The 2026-06-19 evaluation (eval/bm25-chunk-spike/analyzer-and-efsearch-findings.md) showed the code-aware analyzer (WordDelimiter: camelCase + snake_case splitting) lets BM25 match identifier/code-symbol queries - but only pays off under a BM25-heavy fusion, which collapses natural-language recall. So it stays 'standard' globally; 'code' is for a future query-adaptive routing path, not a global flip. (Pairs with the bm25_weight/truncate knobs above.) |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_enabled` | When enabled, comparative/multi-part queries are split into 2-4 sub-queries by the local LLM (fail-closed to single-pass on any error, and forced off whenever wikantik.genai.mode disallows chat inference), retrieved separately, and RRF-fused. Targets cross-page comparative ("X vs Y") queries. This whole wikantik.bundle.decomposition.* family is read by prefix (BundleDecompositionConfig.PREFIX) - these are declared examples at the real defaults, not commented-out placeholders. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.model` | `string` | `gemma4-assist:latest` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_model` | Ollama model used for query decomposition when enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.base_url` | `url` | `http://inference.jakefear.com:11434` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_base_url` | Ollama base URL for the decomposition model; only consulted when enabled=true. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.timeout_ms` | `long` | `4000` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_timeout_ms` | Per-call decomposition HTTP timeout, in milliseconds. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.max_subqueries` | `int` | `4` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_max_subqueries` | Cap on the number of sub-queries the planner may return. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.rrf_k` | `double` | `60` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_rrf_k` | Reciprocal-rank-fusion constant used when merging sub-query result sets. |
| `wikantik.bundle.decomposition.fusion` | `enum(rrf\|roundrobin)` | `rrf` | `wikantik_bundle_decomposition_fusion` | Fusion strategy for sub-query result sets: rrf (score-summed, amplifies the majority topic - measured to hurt multi-hop recall) or roundrobin (reserves per-sub-query position so the minority side of a comparative query survives the top-N cut). |

These two values mirror that unshipped tail so ExpectedCtrCurve.fromTable can still answer for positions beyond the table; they must be updated by hand if jakemon's own opportunities.py _DEEP_CTR / page-2-floor cutoff ever changes. |
| `wikantik.insights.ctr.deep_max_position` | `int` | `20` | `wikantik_insights_ctr_deep_max_position` | Last position ctr.deep applies to flat; deeper positions decay. |

## Connectors

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wikantik.connectors.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `wikantik_connectors_enabled` | Registers properties- and DB-backed (admin UI at /admin/connectors) connectors and, unless disabled below, runs their periodic due-tick syncs. Manual trigger + status at /admin/connectors/*. An empty connector set (no properties keys, no DB rows) is a harmless no-op either way, so this only needs to be set to false to hard-disable syncing (e.g. a read replica); config CRUD via the admin UI keeps working even when disabled. Default ON - this is a kill switch, not an opt-in. |
| `wikantik.connectors.sync.interval.hours` | `int` | `0` | `wikantik_connectors_sync_interval_hours` | Per-connector sync interval, in hours, used by properties-origin connectors (a DB-backed connector's interval is set from /admin/connectors instead). <= 0 means manual-only: the due-tick scheduler never syncs the connector automatically, only when triggered by hand. |
| `wikantik.connectors.egress.allowPrivate` | `boolean` | `false` | `-Dwikantik.connectors.egress.allowPrivate` only | SSRF egress policy for connector HTTP fetches (web crawler, sitemap, feed, GitHub, Confluence). false rejects any host that resolves to loopback/private/link-local/multicast/IPv6-ULA, on every redirect hop too. Set true only for a deliberate internal crawl (e.g. an intranet Confluence). Read only as a JVM system property (-Dwikantik.connectors.egress.allowPrivate=true); this file's value is not consulted. |
| `wikantik.connectors.crypto.key` | `secret` | *(blank)* | `wikantik_connectors_crypto_key` | Connector credential encryption (P2.2). Base64-encoded 32-byte AES-256 master key. An invalid key (wrong length/encoding) is also treated as absent, logged with a warning - the key value itself is never logged. Generate: openssl rand -base64 32 cannot be authorised, and admin /admin/connector-credentials returns 503. |

The following settings come from `wikantik-admin-mcp/src/main/resources/wikantik-mcp.properties` (bundled in the wikantik-admin-mcp jar, overlaid by a same-named file in `tomcat/lib/`).

## REST API, MCP & agent surfaces

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp.server.name` | `string` | `wikantik-mcp` | `mcp_server_name` | MCP server identity |
| `mcp.server.title` | `string` | `Wikantik Knowledge Base` | `mcp_server_title` | Human-readable title shown to MCP clients. |
| `mcp.server.version` | `string` | `2.0.0` | `mcp_server_version` | Server version string advertised to MCP clients. |
| `mcp.instructions.file` | `path` | *(blank: the bundled classpath instructions resource is served)* | `mcp_instructions_file` | Instructions text served by the MCP server. By default the bundled /wikantik-mcp-instructions.txt classpath resource is served. To override with a filesystem file (e.g. an operator-edited copy outside the WAR), set this to an ABSOLUTE path, e.g. /opt/wikantik/wikantik-mcp-instructions.txt. Relative paths are NOT supported - the code resolves them against the JVM working dir, which is rarely useful, and quietly falls back to the bundled resource instead. An unreadable configured file also falls back to the bundled resource. |

## MCP access

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp.access.allowedCidrs` | `list` | *(blank: no CIDR allowlist; only API keys (or allowUnrestricted) grant access)* | `mcp_access_allowedCidrs` | Access control - a request passes if it matches EITHER a DB-minted API key OR a source IP within one of these comma-separated CIDR blocks. Generate DB-backed keys via the admin UI at /admin/apikeys (scope=mcp or scope=all). Those keys are bound to a Wikantik principal so JAAS/ACLs apply to each call exactly as they would for that user's interactive session. |
| `mcp.access.allowUnrestricted` | `boolean` | `false` | `mcp_access_allowUnrestricted` | *** SECURITY *** When neither a DB-minted API key nor mcp.access.allowedCidrs grants a request, the filter fails closed: every MCP request is rejected with HTTP 503 and a CRITICAL line is logged at startup. Setting this to true disables both checks (for a trusted local deployment) and treats every MCP caller as a superuser. The integration test suite sets this to true; production deployments must leave it false. |

Raise it only if legitimate distinct callers regularly exceed this count; excess entries are simply not rate-limited. |

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tools.access.allowedCidrs` | `list` | *(blank: no CIDR allowlist; only API keys (or tools.access.allowUnrestricted) grant access.)* | `tools_access_allowedCidrs` | Access control - a request passes if it matches EITHER a DB-minted API key (scope=tools or scope=all, minted via the admin UI at /admin/apikeys) OR a source IP within one of these comma-separated CIDR blocks. |
| `tools.access.allowUnrestricted` | `boolean` | `false` | `tools_access_allowUnrestricted` | *** SECURITY *** When neither a DB-minted API key nor tools.access.allowedCidrs grants a request, the filter fails closed: every tool request is rejected with HTTP 503 and a CRITICAL line is logged at startup. Setting this to true disables both checks (for a trusted local deployment) and treats every caller as authorized. The integration test suite sets this to true; production deployments must leave it false. |

## Tools limits

| Key | Type | Default | Override | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tools.ratelimit.global` | `int` | `100` | `tools_ratelimit_global` | Global rate limit, requests per second, across all /tools/* callers combined. ToolsRateLimiter treats <= 0 as "disabled" for this limit. |
| `tools.ratelimit.perClient` | `int` | `10` | `tools_ratelimit_perClient` | Per-client rate limit, requests per second (client = resolved caller identity). ToolsRateLimiter treats <= 0 as "disabled" for this limit. |
